prerequisites: Physics in 2nd year of high school
Prior mathematical knowledge of vector calculus, trigonometry, and differentiation and integration of single-variable functions

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the concept of wave and know both its mathematical characterization and basic wave phenomena.
Know the basic concepts and laws of electromagnetism and apply them to the analysis of simple electromagnetic situations in vacuum and in material media.
Correctly handle the recommended physical symbology, both in terms of magnitudes and units.
Learn and apply problem-solving strategies related to the different contents of the course.
Acquire skills related to laboratory work and the treatment of measurements and errors.
Knowledge of basic and technological subjects, enabling students to learn new methods and technologies, and providing great versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities, understanding the ethical and professional responsibility of their activity.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the corresponding field of Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment, and solidarity.
Ability to work in a team.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of waves and electromagnetism and their application to solving engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: Electrostatics: Electric charge, Coulomb's Law, Electrostatic field and potential, Charge distributions, Electric dipole, Gauss's Law, Conductors, Capacitors, Electric field energy, Dielectrics.
Electric Current: Electric current intensity and density, Ohm's Law, Resistance, Joule effect, Generators: Electromotive force, DC circuits.

Magnetostatics: Magnetic field, Lorentz Law: Magnetic induction, Hall effect, Magnetic force on an electric current, Magnetic field moment on a loop, Biot-Savart Law, Force between currents, Ampere's Theorem, Magnetic field energy, Magnetism in matter.
Time-varying electromagnetic fields: Electromagnetic induction: Faraday-Henry Law, Self-induction, Maxwell's Equations, RLC circuits, Electrical oscillations.
Oscillations: Free oscillations, Damped oscillations, Forced oscillations.
Waves: Generalities. Mechanical Waves: Concept of wave, Wave differential equation, Classification of waves, Harmonic waves, Mechanical waves, Wave phenomena, Doppler effect.
Practical 2. Capacitor Charging / Magnetic Field of a Solenoid.
Practical 4. Mechanical Waves / Standing Waves on a String.
teaching_methods: Exposition and explanation of theoretical contents by the professor
Illustration of course contents and resolution of typical problems by the professor
Presentation and defense of problems, assignments, projects
Use of simulation software and/or experimental data processing
Analysis of results and preparation of practical reports
Evaluation activities in very small groups
Study of theoretical-practical contents presented in class and laboratory by the professor
Problem solving and preparation of practical reports, assignments, etc. proposed by the professor for individual or group work
Use of the University of Oviedo virtual platform
assessment_rules: For ordinary examination, if minimums for Partial Exam (T1) and Partial Exam (T2) are met, the theory grade is (0.35 x T1) + (0.40 x T2) + (0.10 x PA). If the T1 minimum is not met, theory grade is (0.75 x ET) + (0.10 x PA). Practical work (P1) and Practical Exam (P2) contribute to the practical grade: (0.08 x P1) + (0.07 x P2). A minimum of 5/10 is required for T1, 4/10 for T2 and ET. For approval, 75% attendance to practical sessions is mandatory. The final grade is Theory + Practicals if all minimums and attendance are met, otherwise, it's the minimum of the calculated grade and 4.0. For the extraordinary examination, the theory grade is (0.75 x ET) + (0.10 x PA) with a minimum of 4/10 for ET; practicals grade is either (0.08 x P1) + (0.07 x P2) if attendance is >= 75%, or (0.15 x P2) with a minimum of 4/10 for P2 if attendance is < 75%.
